concerns: The English loanword “wireless” is also used in technology contexts in both varieties.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers directly mean using radio communication instead of cables.

preference_risk.rationale: The English form “wireless” is plausibly ordinary in technology usage in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay.

response.rationale: “Nirkabel” is the ordinary Indonesian term, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “tanpa wayar” for communication without cables. Both fit the same wireless-technology sense, though “wireless” is also widely understood and used in both contexts.
response.risk_rationale: Usage of the English loanword “wireless” may be common enough in both countries to reduce the contrast in informal technology contexts.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Wireless” is a plausible everyday technology term in both Indonesia and Malaysia, so it can weaken the national preference suggested by the pair, although “nirkabel” and “tanpa wayar” remain credible localized choices.
